content: In the field of public health, a big killer refers to a disease or other significant cause of human mortality. Below is a detailed breakdown of global deaths as reported by the World Health Organization (WHO), categorized by specific diseases, conditions, and broader categories: Deaths by Specific Diseases and Conditions: 1. Ischaemic Heart Disease: Responsible for 7,208,000 deaths, accounting for 13% of global mortality. This condition involves reduced blood flow to the heart, often due to coronary artery disease. 2. Cerebrovascular Disease: Causes 5,509,000 deaths, or 10% of global deaths. This includes strokes and other conditions affecting blood flow to the brain. 3. Lower Respiratory Tract Infections: Lead to 3,884,000 deaths, representing 7% of global mortality. These include pneumonia and bronchitis. 4. HIV/AIDS: Results in 2,777,000 deaths, or 5% of global deaths. This is caused by the human immunodeficiency virus, which weakens the immune system. 5. Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD): Accounts for 2,748,000 deaths, or 5% of global mortality. This group of lung diseases includes emphysema and chronic bronchitis. 6. Perinatal Conditions: Cause 2,462,000 deaths, or 4% of global deaths. These include complications such as low birth weight, birth asphyxia, and birth trauma. 7. Diarrhoeal Diseases: Responsible for 1,798,000 deaths, or 3% of global mortality. These are often caused by infections leading to severe dehydration. 8. Tuberculosis (TB): Results in 1,566,000 deaths, or 3% of global deaths. TB is a bacterial infection primarily affecting the lungs. 9. Malaria: Causes 1,272,000 deaths, or 2% of global mortality. This parasitic disease is transmitted by mosquitoes. 10. Trachea, Bronchus, and Lung Cancers: Account for 1,243,000 deaths, or 2% of global deaths. These are among the most common and deadly cancers. 11. Road Traffic Accidents: Lead to 1,192,000 deaths, or 2% of global mortality. These are a major cause of unintentional injuries. 12. Childhood Diseases: Such as pertussis, polio, diphtheria, measles, and tetanus, result in 1,124,000 deaths, or 2% of global deaths. 13. Diabetes Mellitus: Causes 988,000 deaths, or 2% of global mortality. This chronic condition affects blood sugar regulation. 14. Other Unintentional Injuries: Excluding road traffic accidents, poisoning, falls, fires, and drowning, these account for 923,000 deaths, or 2% of global deaths. 15. Hypertensive Heart Disease: Results in 911,000 deaths, or 2% of global mortality. 16. Self-Inflicted Injuries (Suicide): Lead to 873,000 deaths, or 2% of global deaths. 17. Stomach Cancer: Causes 850,000 deaths, or 2% of global mortality. 18. Cirrhosis of the Liver: Results in 786,000 deaths, or 1% of global deaths. This is often caused by chronic alcohol use or hepatitis infections. 19. Nephritis and Nephrosis: Account for 677,000 deaths, or 1% of global mortality. These are kidney-related diseases. 20. Colon and Rectal Cancer: Cause 622,000 deaths, or 1% of global deaths. 21. Liver Cancer: Results in 618,000 deaths, or 1% of global mortality. 22. Violence: Causes 559,000 deaths, or 1% of global deaths. 23. Breast Cancer: Accounts for 477,000 deaths, or 1% of global mortality. 24. Esophageal Cancer: Results in 446,000 deaths, or 1% of global deaths. 25. Inflammatory Heart Disease: Causes 404,000 deaths, or 1% of global mortality. 26. Alzheimer’s Disease and Other Dementias: Lead to 397,000 deaths, or 1% of global deaths. 27. Falls: Account for 392,000 deaths, or 1% of global mortality. Deaths by Broader Categories: 1. Cardiovascular Diseases: Responsible for 16,733,000 deaths, or 27% of global mortality. This includes heart attacks, strokes, and other heart-related conditions. 2. Infectious and Parasitic Diseases: Cause 10,904,000 deaths, or 19% of global deaths. This category includes diseases like HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, and malaria. 3. Malignant Neoplasms (Cancers): Account for 7,121,000 deaths, or 13% of global mortality. 4. Respiratory Infections: Lead to 3,963,000 deaths, or 7% of global deaths. These include lower respiratory tract infections. 5. Respiratory Diseases: Cause 3,702,000 deaths, or 7% of global mortality. This includes COPD and other chronic lung conditions. 6. Unintentional Injuries: Account for 3,551,000 deaths, or 6% of global deaths. These include road traffic accidents, falls, and other accidental injuries. 7. Perinatal Conditions: Result in 2,462,000 deaths, or 4% of global mortality. 8. Digestive Diseases: Cause 1,968,000 deaths, or 4% of global deaths. This includes liver cirrhosis and other gastrointestinal conditions. 9. Intentional Injuries: Lead to 1,618,000 deaths, or 3% of global mortality. This includes violence and suicide. 10. Neuropsychiatric Disorders: Account for 1,112,000 deaths, or 2% of global deaths. This includes Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias. 11. Diabetes Mellitus: Causes 988,000 deaths, or 2% of global mortality. 12. Diseases of the Genitourinary System: Result in 848,000 deaths, or 2% of global deaths. This includes kidney-related conditions. 13. Maternal Conditions: Lead to 510,000 deaths, or 1% of global mortality. These are complications related to pregnancy and childbirth. 14. Congenital Abnormalities: Cause 493,000 deaths, or 1% of global deaths. These are birth defects present from birth. 15. Nutritional Deficiencies: Account for 485,000 deaths, or 1% of global mortality. This includes conditions like severe malnutrition. 16. Nutritional and Endocrine Disorders: Also result in 485,000 deaths, or 1% of global deaths. These statistics are derived from the World Health Organization's 2004 report, which provides a comprehensive analysis of global mortality rates.
